decisions.reason: Although it was not observed on the website after 2019, this distributed airfield lighting control unit sits close to the firm's core integrated airfield systems business, so it is more likely to be retained, updated or folded into a broader offer than fully withdrawn.

The surveillance display supports the firm's data-driven integration strategy, but its later non-observation on the website raises a meaningful chance of discontinuation or absorption into another surveillance product line rather than continued standalone marketing.

Training programs fit the firm's service-heavy airport solutions model and help lock in customer relationships, so absent contrary evidence they are likely to continue even if branding or delivery format changes.

A ground-lighting training course complements installed systems and maintenance services, and such niche training offers are often kept as part of the broader service portfolio rather than explicitly promoted every year.

Airport collaboration software directly matches the firm's stated move toward integrated, intelligent and collaborative operations, making it a strategically important offer that is unlikely to be dropped soon.

As a flagship multilateration surveillance system aligned with the firm's innovation direction and airport capacity and safety goals, it is the least likely of these products to be taken off the market within the coming year.
